paragraphs.title: Opening the Psalm and Recognizing Sin

easy.explanation: The title identifies it as “A Psalm of David.”
easy.q: To whom is the psalm attributed?

easy.explanation: David begins, “Have mercy upon me, O God.”
easy.q: From whom does David ask for mercy?

easy.explanation: He asks God to “blot out my transgressions.”
easy.q: What does David ask God to blot out?

answers: He remains continually aware of his sin
medium.explanation: David says his sin is continually before him.
medium.q: What does “my sin is ever before me” show about David?

answers: He seeks forgiveness and cleansing from sin
He wants to hide his sin from others
medium.explanation: He asks both for mercy and to be washed and cleansed.
medium.q: What connection is there between David’s request for mercy and his request for cleansing?

medium.explanation: David asks God to blot out his sinful acts.
medium.q: What does the word “transgressions” mean in this passage?

answers: To emphasize his responsibility before God
To say that he did nothing wrong
To ask the prophet for help
challenge.explanation: David acknowledges his guilt before God and does not evade responsibility.
challenge.q: Why does David say, “Against thee, thee only, have I sinned”?

answers: David says God’s judgment is unfair
David accepts the righteousness of God’s words and judgment
David asks for all judgment to be canceled
challenge.explanation: David says God is justified when He speaks and clear when He judges.
challenge.q: What is the connection between acknowledging sin and God’s judgment?

answers: A request for mercy, recognition of sin, and acceptance of God’s judgment
challenge.explanation: These are the main movements in the opening verses.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the opening of the psalm?

paragraphs.title: The Defilement of Sin and the Request for Purification

easy.explanation: David says, “thou desirest truth in the inward parts.”
easy.q: What does David ask God to make known to him?

easy.explanation: He says, “Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean.”
easy.q: With what does David ask to be purged?

easy.explanation: He asks, “Make me to hear joy and gladness.”
easy.q: What does David hope to hear after purification?

medium.explanation: The whiteness of snow represents thorough purification.
medium.q: What does the image “whiter than snow” emphasize?

answers: The first describes the cleansing act and the second its result
Both concern the building of Jerusalem
medium.explanation: David asks to be cleansed and then describes the resulting purity.
medium.q: What is the relationship between “Purge me with hyssop” and “wash me”?

medium.explanation: Hyssop is presented as an instrument or symbol of cleansing.
medium.q: What is hyssop in this passage?

answers: Sin is viewed as a condition requiring thorough cleansing
challenge.explanation: The cleansing language emphasizes the depth of purification David seeks.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David’s requests to be purged and washed?

answers: Both concern recognition of the human inner condition
challenge.explanation: David describes his sinful condition and asks God to reveal truth within him.
challenge.q: How are the verses about being shapen in iniquity related to the request for inward truth?

answers: David expects to return to a clean and liberated condition
He wants to replace the sacrifices
challenge.explanation: Joy and gladness are presented as the hoped-for result of purification.
challenge.q: Why does joy appear after the request for cleansing?

paragraphs.title: Renewal of the Heart and Spirit

easy.explanation: David prays, “Create in me a clean heart, O God.”
easy.q: What does David ask God to create in him?

easy.explanation: He asks, “take not thy holy spirit from me.”
easy.q: What does David ask God not to take from him?

easy.explanation: He says, “Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation.”
easy.q: What does David ask God to restore to him?

medium.explanation: David asks for both purity of heart and spiritual steadfastness.
medium.q: What connection exists between “a clean heart” and “a right spirit”?

answers: He wants to remain in God’s presence
He wants to get away from God
He wants to go to war
medium.explanation: The request expresses his desire to continue before God.
medium.q: Why does David ask not to be cast away from God’s presence?

medium.explanation: David asks God to uphold him with His free spirit.
medium.q: What does David ask God’s free spirit to do?

answers: The heart concerns purity, while the spirit concerns steadfastness and faithfulness
The heart concerns the city, while the spirit concerns sacrifice
There is no difference between them
challenge.explanation: The two requests express different aspects of inner renewal.
challenge.q: What is the difference between asking for a clean heart and asking for a right spirit?

answers: Joy and sustaining spiritual strength help David recover after sin
Joy is meant to conceal the sin
challenge.explanation: David asks for renewed joy and inner support after his failure.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the connection between the joy of salvation and a free spirit?

answers: A clean heart, continued presence with God, and restored joy of salvation
Sacrifice, war, and building a wall
Teaching sinners, confession, and destroying Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: This sequence follows the order of David’s petitions.
challenge.q: Which order best describes David’s requests in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Repentance as Testimony and a Way of Life

easy.explanation: He says, “Then will I teach transgressors thy ways.”
easy.q: What does David promise to teach transgressors?
From what does David ask to be delivered?

answers: A broken spirit and a broken and contrite heart
easy.explanation: God does not despise “a broken and a contrite heart.”
easy.q: What kind of sacrifice will God not despise?

answers: So that he may speak and teach from a personally restored condition
So that he can hide his sin
So that he can end the prayer
medium.explanation: After deliverance, David says his tongue will sing of God’s righteousness.
medium.q: Why does David ask for deliverance before speaking of God’s righteousness?

answers: An inwardly broken heart is more important than an outward sacrifice alone
medium.explanation: The passage emphasizes genuine repentance rather than external ritual by itself.
medium.q: What does the contrast between sacrifice and a broken heart teach?

answers: A humbled and broken heart marked by repentance
A heart filled only with celebration
medium.explanation: The phrase describes inward brokenness and remorse.
medium.q: What does “a contrite heart” mean here?

answers: He plans to teach transgressors God’s ways and lead sinners back to Him
He asks to punish every sinner
He asks never to speak again
challenge.explanation: David intends to use his restored relationship with God to teach others.
challenge.q: How does David’s repentance become a testimony to others?

answers: When God opens his lips, David will be able to praise Him
His lips are intended only for eating
challenge.explanation: David says, “O Lord, open thou my lips; and my mouth shall shew forth thy praise.”
challenge.q: What is the connection between opened lips and declaring God’s praise?

answers: It involves confession, a broken heart, and a contrite spirit, not sacrifice alone
It is obtained through wealth alone
It has nothing to do with the human heart
challenge.explanation: The passage places inward repentance at the center of restored fellowship with God.
challenge.q: What view of atonement emerges from these verses?

paragraphs.title: Restoration of the Community and Sacrifices after Atonement

easy.explanation: David prays, “Do good in thy good pleasure unto Zion.”
easy.q: For whom does David ask God to do good?

easy.explanation: He asks, “build thou the walls of Jerusalem.”
easy.q: What does David ask God to build?

answers: Sacrifices of righteousness, burnt offering, and whole burnt offering
easy.explanation: The passage names sacrifices of righteousness, burnt offering, and whole burnt offering.
easy.q: What sacrifices are mentioned at the altar?

answers: Both express restoration and blessing for the community
Both describe only David’s personal sin
medium.explanation: David asks for both Zion’s good and Jerusalem’s restoration.
medium.q: What is the connection between doing good to Zion and building Jerusalem’s walls?

answers: After the requested restoration of Zion and Jerusalem
medium.explanation: “Then” connects the acceptable sacrifices with the preceding restoration.
medium.q: When will the sacrifices of righteousness be acceptable?

answers: An offering consumed completely on the altar
medium.explanation: The phrase identifies a sacrifice wholly offered on the altar.
medium.q: What does “whole burnt offering” mean in this passage?

answers: The requested restoration includes the welfare of the whole community
The psalm is only about construction
challenge.explanation: The conclusion expands David’s concern from personal restoration to communal blessing.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the movement from personal sin to Zion and Jerusalem?

answers: The sacrifices follow the requested restoration and forgiveness
The sacrifices come before recognition of sin
The sacrifices are unrelated to the process
challenge.explanation: “Then” marks the sacrifices as following the restoration described earlier.
challenge.q: What does the word “Then” emphasize in the final verse?

answers: As expressions of righteousness and willing devotion after restoration
As substitutes for a broken heart
As a way to conceal sin
challenge.explanation: The sacrifices appear after repentance and restoration and are called sacrifices of righteousness.
challenge.q: How are the sacrifices portrayed at the end of the psalm?
